To understand why, wedevelop a tractable static bargaining model of family long-term-care choices and estimateit using European data. Families choose among child-provided informal care,including which child becomes the caregiver, formal home care, mixed care, and nursing-homecare, taking into account both monetary costs and heterogeneous non-monetarypreferences over care arrangements. Preference heterogeneity strongly dampens policyresponsiveness: without it, a 20% subsidy to nursing-home and formal-home-care costsraises the use of formal care by 7.5%, compared with only 4.0% in the baseline model.Cross-country differences in care arrangements are shaped more by non-monetary factorsthan by formal-care prices. Looking ahead, the model predicts a substantial increasein demand for formal care by 2050, driven by a declining ratio of adult children toelderly parents, with the largest increases in countries where informal care is currentlypredominant.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7126885\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5204/thesis.eprints.268426\", \"title\": [\"Long-Term Generative Models for Multimodal Behavior in Soccer\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This thesis develops deep learning algorithms for modelling long-term behaviours in soccer, spanning both continuous player and ball motion and the discrete actions that structure a match. These models address two long-standing industry-level challenges: collecting complete trajectories across all televised games, and labelling actions in those games in a semi-automated manner. The methods developed in this thesis have been deployed commercially, substantially increasing the scale and efficiency of soccer data collection.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5204/thesis.eprints.268426\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.21511/imfi.18(2).2021.18\…
